prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs (budget, timing, home size, ductwork condition, brand preference). To give a tailored recommendation I’ll need your ZIP code and any preferences. Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide and next steps so you can pick a great contractor.

What I can do for you
- If you give your ZIP code I’ll find 3–5 highly rated local HVAC companies, summarize recent reviews, note certifications (NATE/manufacturer), warranty/financing options, and any red flags.
- Or I can give a checklist and script to use when getting quotes so you can compare bids yourself.

How to pick the best company (checklist)
1. Get at least 3 written, itemized estimates (equipment, labor, permits, disposal). Don’t accept a vague “single price.”
2. Ask for a Manual J load calculation and (if needed) Manual D duct design — this ensures correctly sized equipment.
3. Verify credentials:
   - NATE-certified technicians
   - Manufacturer dealer/installer certification (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.) if you want a specific brand
   - Liability insurance and worker’s comp
   - Local license/registration (ask for license numbers)
4. Compare warranties: equipment vs. labor vs. parts, and any required registration for extended manufacturer warranty.
5. Check reviews and complaints: Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and BBB. Look for consistent patterns (reliability, timeliness, honoring warranties).
6. Ask about permits and inspections — a proper installation needs local permits.
7. Confirm removal/disposal of old equipment and whether they’ll reconnect/modify ducts or thermostat.
8. Request a written start and completion date and a final commissioning checklist (safety checks, airflow readings, refrigerant charge).
9. Look for energy-efficiency advice: recommended SEER rating, expected monthly energy use, and available utility rebates.
10. Financing and payment terms: ask about deposits, financing options, and lien waivers.

Questions to ask every contractor (copy/paste)
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your license number?
- Are your installers NATE-certified or manufacturer-certified?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and provide the report?
- What equipment brand and model do you recommend and why? What is the SEER rating?
- What exactly is included in the written estimate? (parts, labor, permits, disposal)
- What are the equipment and labor warranties? Any conditions to keep warranty valid?
- Do you handle permits and inspections?
- Who will perform the installation? (employee vs. subcontractor)
- How long will the job take? What’s the start date?
- Can you provide 2–3 recent local references?

Companies to consider in Atlanta
- Large regional/national companies commonly used in Atlanta include Coolray, R.S. Andrews, and One Hour Heating & Air. These often have wide service coverage and multiple technicians. I can verify up‑to‑date ratings for your exact area if you give your ZIP code.

Next step
Tell me your ZIP code, any brand or budget preferences, and whether you need the job done urgently. I’ll pull 3–5 top local options, summarize their reviews/certifications, and suggest which to call first.
